The study of marine ecosystems helps scientists understand the complex relationships between 
ocean organisms and their environments.

Coral reefs, for example, support a large variety of 
marine species and play a crucial role in maintaining biodiversity.
Oceanographers examine how temperature, salinity, and ocean currents affect marine life.

These environmental factors influence migration patterns, breeding behavior, and the 
distribution of many aquatic species.

Protecting marine ecosystems is important for maintaining global biodiversity and supporting 
sustainable fisheries.

Conservation efforts often focus on reducing pollution, protecting habitats, 
and managing fishing practices responsibly.
